strengths.subject: Security

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: The only external input in the files in scope is SystemController.About's show-details query parameter, which is strongly typed as bool via [FromQuery]/[BindRequired] model binding (invalid values are rejected before the action runs); TestingController.ResetTesting and TestingRepository.ResetTestingAsync take no user-supplied data at all.

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: TestingRepository.ResetTestingAsync executes only the fixed constants SqlConstants.SqlServerResetTestingScript / PostgreSqlResetTestingScript; no request, config, or other external value is concatenated or interpolated into any SQL text.

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: Data access uses Dapper's CommandDefinition/QueryFirstOrDefaultAsync (a vetted parameterized-query API) against SqlConnection/NpgsqlConnection; no ADO.NET command text is built by string concatenation.

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: No shell/OS process execution (Process.Start or similar) exists in TestingRepository.cs, SqlConstants.cs, TestingController.cs or SystemController.cs.

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: None of the files in scope perform XML parsing (no XmlReader/XmlDocument/XDocument usage).

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: None of the files in scope implement file upload handling (no IFormFile parameters or storage code).

checkResults.subject: Security
checkResults.reason: No file upload/storage code exists in the files in scope, so there is no upload location whose executability to assess.

notes: Reviewed TestingRepository.cs, Constants/SqlConstants.cs, TestingController.cs and SystemController.cs. SQL injection surface is effectively absent in this batch: TestingRepository executes fixed constant scripts via Dapper's parameterized CommandDefinition with no user-controlled data reaching SQL text, and connection-string interpolation uses only application configuration (not external request input), so it falls outside this checklist's scope. XML parsing and file-upload checks (SEC-II-05/06/07) are N/A because those capabilities are not present in the files reviewed; a repo-wide scan may find them elsewhere outside this batch's scope.
